title: Kyno Update 1
changes: Point your camera at a question and Kyno reads it, checks it, and sends it to the Solver.
Camera Study now answers the way your NCERT textbook does — same terms, same steps, with the chapter it came from.
Chemical equations are balanced by actually solving them, so the coefficients are right every time.
The Formula Reader matches what it sees against your own formula sheet.
Your streak now survives one missed day a week instead of resetting to zero.
Your streak, XP and level read the same number everywhere in the app.
Topics you study get filed under the right subject — Quadratic Equations is Maths again, not Chemistry.
Tools that were not finished yet are no longer shown as if they were.
Notification settings actually apply now, and split by the kind of reminder.

title: Kyno Update 2
changes: Every button in Kyno now looks and presses the same way, so the main action on a screen is obvious.
You will see this card after logging in whenever there is something new — including anything you missed.

title: Kyno Update 3
changes: Answers now match your grade as well as your board — a Class 6 explanation is no longer a Class 9 explanation with the same words.
IB is now a full option with its own topic lists, alongside CBSE and Cambridge.
Switched board? A new page compares your old and new curriculum and shows exactly what you still need to catch up on.
Your formula sheets and revision drills now follow your own curriculum instead of one universal list.

title: Kyno Update 4
changes: Revision Reels: swipe through your own formulas and flashcards — cards due for review come up first, and it remembers where you stopped.
Every solved doubt now has a Save to Reels button, so a good explanation becomes a revision card in one tap.
Explain it differently: one tap gets you a genuinely new angle on the same doubt, not the same words reshuffled.
Search your past doubts from the sidebar — it looks inside the answers too, not just your questions.
New Define camera button: snap any word you don't know for a plain-language meaning at your grade level.

title: Kyno Update 5
changes: Home now opens with Today's 3 things — three small tasks picked from what you're about to forget, your weakest topic, and what's due, each with the reason why.
A personal progress line compares you only with yourself — accuracy this week vs three weeks ago, never with other students.
Revision drills now open at the difficulty your recent answers earned, one step at a time — you can always override it.

title: Kyno Update 6
changes: Kyno OS now shows where your time actually went — real minutes per subject and chapter from Reels, Solver answers and finished drills, never an estimate.
After a rough drill, you get a recovery plan built from that attempt's own wrong answers: what to re-learn, what just needs practice, and what's already solid.

title: Kyno Update 7
changes: Kyno works offline now — once you've opened it, the app loads without internet, and everything you've saved was already on your device.
Starting a topic whose earlier chapter gave you trouble? Kyno offers a quick brush-up first — your call, never a lock.
Fell behind your exam plan? One tap re-fits the missed blocks over the days you have left, most important first, without overloading any day.

title: Kyno Update 8
changes: Study Rooms: create a room, share the 6-letter code, and study on one shared Pomodoro with a live list of who's in — anyone in the room can start or pause for everyone.
If the AI mentors are ever too busy, your daily brief no longer breaks — Kyno builds the plan from your own data and says so.

title: Kyno Update 9
changes: Study Rooms now have a shared notes wall — post a note everyone in the room sees live, and save any note straight into your own Notebook to keep it.
Rooms hold a big group now — study together with the shared timer and notes.

title: Kyno Update 10
changes: Revision Reels now start you off with ready-made decks — high-yield Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Maths cards you can add in one tap, so there's something to revise from day one.
Added decks join your own cards and get spaced out for review like everything else.

title: Kyno Update 11
changes: Camera Study can now quiz you on diagram labels — snap a diagram, recall each part from its clue, then reveal.
Mistake Analysis now shows WHY you miss questions — careless slips, concept gaps or time pressure — each with what to do about it.
Any solved doubt can become fill-in-the-blank cards in one tap.
New 'Which stream?' guide (Class 9-10): a Science/Commerce/Arts suggestion weighed against how you actually perform, not just a quiz.

title: Kyno Update 12
changes: My goal: set your board target once and Kyno tracks the gap per subject from how you actually score — plus the exact topics that win back the most marks.
Focus Lock: a study timer where only real focus counts — drift to another app and the clock calmly waits. Builds a focus streak from your real sessions.
The Mistake Museum: every wrong answer files itself with the full question. Re-drill your misses; beat one twice in a row and it retires to Fixed.
Listen: your revision cards read aloud by your device — due cards first, formulas included, works offline. Revise while walking.
Mock test: sit a paper under real exam conditions — a clock that never pauses, OMR answers, negative marking on JEE/NEET patterns, and a post-mortem showing exactly where marks leaked.

title: Kyno Update 13
changes: Focus Lock now takes a ban list — name the apps you're banning (Instagram, games, your call) and Kyno holds you to it: leave for any of them and the clock freezes, the drift is timed, and it all shows on your session receipt.
Every focus session now ends with a receipt of what you ACTUALLY studied in it — questions answered, cards flipped, notes made, topics touched — pulled from your real activity, never self-reported.
Home and Kyno OS show Today's focus: your focused minutes, whether you kept the contract, and what you studied inside the lock.
